description: Harden two timing-fragile e2e tests so the plan-runner preflight full-suite bun test cannot false-positive under CPU contention.

userStories.title: Replace fixed timing budgets with generous waitForCondition/per-test timeouts in the two load-sensitive e2e tests
userStories.description: As a maintainer running the plan-runner preflight, I need the two timing-fragile e2e tests to hold under full-suite CPU contention so the preflight cannot false-positive and silently wedge the autonomous drain.
acceptanceCriteria: The orch-recycle-watch respawn assertion is gated by waitForCondition polling (not a bare fixed setTimeout/sleep timing budget) and its poll budgets plus the outer per-test timeout are generous enough to survive full-suite contention. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'waitForCondition' test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]
The orch-recycle-watch e2e test passes when run on its own. [oracle: bun test test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]

interactivity.test.ts Test 5 ('runInit ... does not throw and exits via the linear print path') has an explicit generous per-test timeout (third arg to test(...)) or polling so it does not exceed its budget under load, rather than relying on Bun's default 5000ms. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
The interactivity test file passes when run on its own. [oracle: bun test test/interactivity/interactivity.test.ts]
No product source is modified: only the two named test files change relative to main (no file outside test/ in the diff). [oracle: file-assert ! git diff --name-only main | grep -qv '^test/']
Assertion correctness is unchanged; only timing sensitivity is relaxed (the respawn UUID-change assertion and the runInit exit-code assertion remain intact). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine is green (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts (~line 213-253; the newUUID-change waitForCondition already uses {timeoutMs:12_000,intervalMs:500} and outer test timeout {timeout:20_000}; the pgrep-scheduled and pgrep-new waitForCondition calls use the helper default timeoutMs=5000 which is too tight under contention) and test/interactivity/interactivity.test.ts (Test 5 at ~line 502, currently relies on Bun's default 5000ms per-test timeout). Helper: test/helpers/wait-for-condition.ts (default timeoutMs=5000, intervalMs=20). Fix: raise the internal waitForCondition budgets on the two default-timeout pgrep waits and the outer 20_000ms test timeout in orch-recycle-watch; add an explicit generous per-test timeout (third arg to test()) to interactivity Test 5. Project invariant (patterns.md 'poll with waitForCondition, never fixed setTimeout'): do not introduce a bare setTimeout budget as the gate. Gotcha: the tests are logically correct and pass in isolation; do NOT weaken any assertion, only the timing sensitivity. Test-only change: touch no src/ file.
